info.title: Map voice roles and AI chat systems (@explore subagent)

parts.text:
Thoroughness: very thorough. Read-only research, no code changes. Repo root: /home/runner/hub-work/yomikai/code (Kotlin/Android, Mihon/Tachiyomi fork named Yomikai).

I need an accurate map of three existing subsystems so I can extend them. Report concrete file paths, class names, function signatures, preference keys, and what already exists vs what is missing. Do NOT speculate — verify by reading code.

SUBSYSTEM 1 — Voice roles / slots / per-voice parameters:
1. Find `VoiceRoleDictionary` (search whole repo; it may live in a different module than app/). Report: its data model (fields incl. pitch/rate/voice/gender), how roles are resolved from a speaker name, and how it is persisted (preference keys, JSON shape).
2. In app/src/main/java/eu/kanade/tachiyomi/data/tts/TtsSpeaker.kt: list every public entry point for speaking (speak, speakAs, speakWithVoice, speakSystem, speakRemote, speakWithEdgeVoice etc.) with signatures, and explain exactly how role -> voice -> pitch/rate is applied, including how gender mismatch between role and chosen voice is (or is not) handled.
3. Find every voice-related preference key in domain/src/main/java/mihon/domain/ocr/service/OcrPreferences.kt (e.g. voiceSlots, voiceFemale, voiceMale, voiceName, voiceEngine, speechRate, speechPitch, manualVoiceGender, voicePresetGender, systemTtsEngine, edgeVoice, elevenVoiceId, ttsWebLanguage...). Give key + type + default value for each.
4. In app/src/main/java/eu/kanade/presentation/reader/TtsSettingsDialog.kt: describe the UI that exists for slots/roles — is there a per-voice pitch/tone/timbre slider? Is there a "test voice" button? Can multiple voices be tested in sequence? Can a voice be saved as a named preset? Quote the relevant composable/function names and line numbers.
5. Search for any concept of a saved/named voice preset (names like VoicePreset, preset, слот, шаблон голоса). Report what exists.
6. Report how the engine picker lists engines+voices today (VoicePlugins.available/voices/systemEngineOptions) and whether multiple different engines can be active simultaneously or only one global engine at a time.

SUBSYSTEM 2 — AI chat sessions and background AI logging:
1. For each file in app/src/main/java/eu/kanade/tachiyomi/data/ai/ (AiAgent, AiAssistant, AiChatTools, AiHistoryManager, AiReaderTools, AiHttpServer, AiWorkspace, ReaderAiActions, AiModelRoles, LocalLlm, BookChatProfile), give a one-to-two line summary of its responsibility and its main public entry points.
2. Is there a persistent "chat session" concept (list of sessions/messages, stored where)? Report the storage mechanism and the data model.
3. Does anything currently write AI activity that happened in the BACKGROUND (e.g. during autoread/OCR) into a chat transcript? Search for logging of background work into a session, and for any "сессия"/"session" naming related to reading or autoread.
4. Is there a mode where the AI is read-only / user can only edit? Report any permission/role concept (AiModelRoles) and how it restricts tools.
5. Report whether the AI can be called per text region / per line during autoread (any hook from AutoReadEngine or OcrRepository into the AI subsystem), and whether the AI receives speaker attribution (who says what, who is addressed).

SUBSYSTEM 3 — Autoread TTS pipeline and speaker attribution:
1. In app/src/main/java/eu/kanade/tachiyomi/data/tts/AutoReadEngine.kt: outline the flow from page -> OCR regions -> text -> TTS, including how speaker name / gender is determined per region (SpeechMarkup.genderOf, speakerName, boxes, vertical text handling), and the streaming path.
2. Report what data is available at the moment a line is spoken: is the speaker name, the addressee, and the surrounding context (previous/next lines) available? Quote the fields.
3. Note the hooks where an AI call could be inserted per line without breaking the 25s frame timeout (OCR_FRAME_TIMEOUT_MS) and the 1.2s TTS start grace (TTS_START_GRACE_MS).

Output format: three sections matching the three subsystems, bullet points, every claim with file:line. End with a short "MISSING" list: what from the user's request (per-voice tone/timbre sliders, saving voices as separate presets, testing several voices in sequence, AI auto-tuning voices per line by speaker/addressee, background AI activity written into a dedicated autoread chat session where the user can only edit) does NOT exist today.

Thoroughness: medium-high. Repo: /home/runner/hub-work/yomikai/code (Android/Kotlin reader "yomihon-custom").

Goal: find every place where offline autoread (авточтение) is started/stopped, and every place that reports TTS (text-to-speech) availability or failure to the user, so I can make autoread stop and warn when the device has no working TTS engine.

Report with file paths + line numbers + short excerpts:

1. Where autoread is started and stopped from the reader UI: search `readFrame(`, `autoRead`, `AutoReadEngine` usages (likely `app/src/main/java/eu/kanade/tachiyomi/ui/reader/ReaderActivity.kt`, `ReaderViewModel.kt`). What user action starts it, and what toasts/snackbar/confirm dialogs exist around it.
2. All existing user-visible feedback mechanisms in the reader: toast helper, snackbar, `TtsReadingNotifier` (app/src/main/java/eu/kanade/tachiyomi/data/tts/TtsReadingNotifier.kt) — what it does, how it posts notifications, what channels/permission it needs.
3. Any existing check of TTS availability/voices: search for `installedEngines`, `systemVoiceSpecs`, `TextToSpeech`, `voices`, `prepareForLanguage`, `VoiceHelper`. Report if there is any "is TTS usable" predicate today.
4. How `TtsSpeaker.speakAs` failures are surfaced today: search for `setSpeaking(false)`, `isSpeaking`, `onState`, and any place that reacts to a failed speak.
5. `data/src/main/java/mihon/data/ocr/OcrHistoryStore.kt` — the `addAutoRead` API and how it is displayed (which screen reads it).
6. Any user-facing setting/preference that lets the user pick the voice engine (`OcrPreferences.voiceEngine`), and where the voice settings screen lives.

Do NOT modify files. Report findings only, organized by question, with file:line references.

Thoroughness: medium-high. Repo: /home/runner/hub-work/yomikai/code (Android/Kotlin, "yomihon-custom" reader).

I need to know exactly how the in-reader AI chat works, to add streaming output (text appears progressively instead of one blob at the end).

Investigate and report with concrete file paths + line numbers + short code excerpts:

1. `app/src/main/java/eu/kanade/tachiyomi/ui/reader/...` — the AI chat overlay UI (ReaderAiChatOverlay.kt or similar): how a message is sent, how the assistant reply is rendered into the message list, whether there is any incremental/partial rendering, and what state holds the current reply.
2. `eu/kanade/tachiyomi/data/ai/AiAssistant.kt` (and related files: AiBackends.kt, AiPlugins.kt, AiAgent.kt if present): how the chat request is made over the network (HttpURLConnection? OkHttp? SSE `stream` parameter anywhere?), whether responses are read fully at once (`readBytes()`/`readText()`), whether there is any callback/flow for partial content, and how the final text is parsed from the response body. Note the exact function signatures used by the UI to send a chat message.
3. Whether any other place in the app already streams (grep for `stream`, `text/event-stream`, `data:`, `flush`, `onChunk`, `Flow<String>`).
4. What models/backends are used for chat (catalogue names) and whether the response format parsing is centralized in one function (so streaming could reuse the same parser per chunk).
5. Also check `domain/` and `data/` for any OCR result streaming/progress API that already exists: `data/src/main/java/mihon/data/ocr/OcrStageBus.kt`, `OcrRepositoryImpl.kt` — report the public API surface for (a) progressive stages/progress, (b) per-region/segment recognition, and any callback hooks.

Do NOT modify any files. Report only findings, organized by the 5 questions, with file:line references.

parts.text:
Repo: /home/runner/hub-work/yomikai/code (Kotlin, Android manga reader "yomikai"/Mihon fork).

I need a "very thorough" analysis of TWO subsystems. Report exact file paths, function signatures, and line numbers.

## 1. AI chat history / sessions (for adding a separate roleplay session)

Read and report on:
- `app/src/main/java/eu/kanade/tachiyomi/data/ai/AiHistoryManager.kt` — full contents summary: the `Msg` data class fields, `load`, `append`, `clear` functions, how the file path is derived (is it per-mangaId? one file per manga? filename format?), and any trimming/limits.
- `app/src/main/java/eu/kanade/tachiyomi/data/ai/BookKnowledge.kt` — specifically `Session` class (if any), `ensureSession`, `load`, `save`, `render` functions, the `Book` data class fields, and the file naming for per-manga JSON.
- `app/src/main/java/eu/kanade/tachiyomi/data/ai/AiAgent.kt` — find the function that builds the `historyBlock` for the prompt (signature, params, how history is truncated/filtered/budgeted), and any place that computes a session id.
- `app/src/main/java/eu/kanade/presentation/reader/components/ReaderAiChatOverlay.kt` — the composable parameters list (top ~120 lines), where `history` is declared/loaded/cleared, and where `sendMessage` is called.
- Anywhere that displays a chat/session history list or a "clear history" action, for both AI chat and general app (grep for `AiHistoryManager`, `clearHistory`, `deleteHistory`).

I need to know: to give roleplay its OWN history (separate from normal chat), what is the minimal change? Does the history file path include anything I could add a "mode" segment to? Is history keyed only by mangaId?

## 2. TTS (text-to-speech) pipeline (for voices, sighs, interjections)

Find and report on the TTS implementation, likely `app/src/main/java/eu/kanade/tachiyomi/data/tts/`:
- `TtsSpeaker.kt` and any other files in that dir.
- For EACH file: what the public API is (classes, objects, functions, their signatures), and especially:
  - How text is PREPARED before being sent to the TTS engine. Look for any regex/cleanup that strips or transforms text: parentheses/brackets content (e.g. `(вздох)`, `[ааа]`, `*шёпотом*`), markdown, emoji, quotes, asterisks, underscores, ellipses, dashes.
  - Whether bracketed/parenthesized stage directions (emotional cues like "вздох", "ааа", "крик", "шёпот", "смеётся") are currently REMOVED or SPOKEN.
  - How the model/voice is selected per sentence or per message (pitch/rate/pan/volume controls if any).
  - Any per-character or per-speaker voice assignment (the AI knows characters, so voices may be assigned per character name).
  - Where TTS is invoked from the AI chat overlay (does the user long-press a message to read it aloud?).
- Also report what TTS engines/options exist (Android TTS? OpenAI-compatible? custom?) and whether pitch/rate/emphasis can be set per utterance.

Quote the exact regex or cleanup code you find, with file path and line numbers, so I can decide how to make interjections spoken instead of dropped.

Do NOT modify any files. This is research only. Return a detailed structured report.

Очень тщательно исследуй Android/Kotlin-репозиторий без изменений. Нужна точная карта для реализации требования: при первом AI/авточтении книги создаётся отдельная книжная AI-сессия; агент может сам найти/прочитать сайт или принять URL/текст от пользователя; изученные правила (порядок чтения, области/рамки, баблы/облачки, роли и голоса) сохраняются и применяются к OCR, авточтению, переводу и озвучке; OCR, чат и оркестратор должны выбираться раздельно и показываться. Найди и прочитай релевантные файлы: ReaderActivity/ViewModel, AutoReadEngine, AiAgent, AiChatTab/ReaderAiChatOverlay, AiHttpServer, BookKnowledge, BooksStore/Book models, OcrPreferences/Settings AI, AiBackends/AiChoices/AI history, web tools, voice resolver, DI. Верни: (1) точные пути и диапазоны строк ключевых функций/типов, (2) текущий поток вызовов при открытии книги и старте авточтения, (3) где уже есть bookId/знания/история и как их расширить минимальным изменением, (4) где выбираются и фактически вызываются модели OCR/chat/orchestrator, (5) точки UI для первого запуска/выбора URL и модели, (6) существующие тестовые паттерны и рекомендуемый безопасный план реализации с разбиением на небольшие коммиты. Не редактируй файлы, не запускай сборку и не коммить. Пиши по-русски, указывай ссылки file:line.

Проведи тщательное исследование кода репозитория без внесения изменений. Найди компоненты «читалки»/reader, взаимодействие AI со страницами книги, получение или обучение на данных из интернета, а также ручной ввод/обучение от пользователя. Проследи поток данных от UI до API/сервисов и обратно, найди связанные модели, промпты, провайдеры, endpoints, хранилища и тесты. Верни краткий, но конкретный отчёт на русском: архитектура, ключевые файлы с номерами строк, что уже реализовано, пробелы/неясности, и какие команды/тесты можно запустить для проверки. Не редактируй файлы и не коммить.
